method:
Seven read-only auditors (A-G) each took a region of the specification (A-F) or the proto's REQUIRED fields (G) and recorded every RFC 2119 statement with the code and tests they opened. Their entries are model output: the ones this branch changed (changed_by) were re-verified by reproducing the defect and showing the new test fail without the fix; the rest are recorded as found and have not been independently re-verified. Notes and citations corrected to match the code without a change to it (2026-10-13) carry no changed_by: they were checked by reading the code, not by a failing test. Re-anchored 2026-10-14 from upstream main at 12e9d2fbb9ba, which the entries were made against, to the v1.0.1 tag: every spec_line, and every spec line number cited in a note, was moved through a line map built from the two texts by difflib (equal runs, and replaced blocks of equal length, map line for line); 191 entries moved, and the three §7.6.4 entries, whose text v1.0.1 does not have, moved to after_release.

Citations made checkable 2026-10-23. Of the 1,484 impl_evidence citations then in the file (1,481 in entries, 3 under after_release), 1,139 were a bare Rust `path:line` that named nothing, 171 named a symbol with or without a line, and the rest were line ranges, prose, or Markdown, TOML, YAML and JSON paths without a line. Every Rust citation is now `path:line Symbol`, the line on which that item is defined, and every other one `path:line "fragment"`, the fragment on that line (one directory, the extension URI-contract snapshots, stays cited whole); duplicates within an entry collapsed, leaving 1,458. A bare line was mapped to the item it sits in or documents (254 already on a definition, 111 on its doc comment or attribute, 394 inside a function, 120 inside a struct, enum or const, 4 on an impl head with one method); the 476 not already on a definition were listed beside their requirement and read, and 26 lines (65 citations) that had pointed at the wrong code from the start, such as builder.rs doc lines that resolve to allow_unauthenticated_extended_card where build() is meant, were re-pointed by hand. The 136 entries an independent audit marked STALE_CITATION, and 47 others whose citation was a range, a blank line, a use, a module header, a brace or the wrong code, were re-pointed after opening the code; a target the auditor named was adopted only once the file showed it. Test citations were re-derived to the line of `fn name` (1,018 already there, 60 moved, most off the `#[test]` line above, 320 given the line they lacked), 50 stronger tests the audit named were added after reading each, one that proves nothing about its clause was dropped, and no status changed. Notes the audit proved stale were corrected in place, each marked 2026-10-23. Checked by scripts/check_spec_ledger.py, which since then refuses any other form, and any line that is not the definition, the `fn` line or the fragment's line, proves those rules on a fixture tree on every run (`--self-test`), and with `--fix-lines` moves a line number whose target is found exactly once.

entries.requirement: A generated JSON artifact (`spec/a2a.json`...) MAY be published for convenience to tooling and the website
entries.notes: Concerns the spec project's documentation build, not an SDK. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: binds the specification project (its documents, website or process), not an implementation.

entries.requirement: SDK language bindings, schemas, and any other derived forms MUST be regenerated from the proto (directly or via code generation) rather than edited manually.
entries.notes: Every public serde type that mirrors a2a.proto is generated from it (ADR 0016, register R49): tools/a2a-codegen (protox, no protoc) writes crates/a2a-protocol-types/src/generated/ from the proto and codegen.toml, which records each deliberate difference with its reason and is refused when it names anything the proto lacks or omits a proto type. All 46 proto types and the PartContent enum are generated; the prost message types come from build.rs. CI's static checks run `a2a-codegen --check` (ci.yml:96), which fails when a generated file differs from what the proto makes (proven by the gate prover with a hand edit to generated/task.rs) and when any Rust file git knows of, outside src/generated/ and the generator, declares a struct, enum, union or type under one of the 47 generated names (shown 2026-10-15 by four injections: a struct in a tracked file, one in an untracked file, a type alias, a pub(crate) enum; each failed naming file and line). The vendored proto copies are checked byte-identical to the v1.0.1 release (check_proto_copies.sh, the two proto_schema_sync tests). The serde-prost conversions are hand-written code, not a derived form: each builds its target with a full struct literal (no `..Default::default()` in src/proto/convert/), so a field the proto adds to either generated side fails to compile until mapped. Not checked mechanically: that a hand-written conversion maps a field correctly, which the conversion round-trip tests and the proto_convert fuzz target cover.

entries.requirement: Migration guidance MUST be provided via an ancillary document when introducing major breaking changes.
entries.notes: Read as the sibling at spec line 115 is read, binding the SDK as well as the specification project (independent re-audit 2026-10-24: both bullets are unattributed passives in one list, and the one between them, 114, names SDKs). entries.requirement: The stream MUST follow one of these patterns: (1) Message-only stream ... (2) Task lifecycle stream
entries.notes: The executor's first event decides the send stream's pattern (InMemoryQueueReader::set_provisional_task): a Message makes a message-only stream, anything else a task stream that begins with the Task. A Message an executor writes once its task stream has begun (after a Task, status or artifact update) is sent, since 2026-10-23, as a TaskStatusUpdateEvent that keeps the state the turn last wrote (or, before any status, the state the turn began in) and carries the message in status.message. The writer folds it once, before the event takes its log position, so the send stream, a SubscribeToTask stream and a resumed replay carry one payload at that position (§3.5.2); the processors store it as a history entry and the status message, with no transition check, and push it. A fold in each stream's reader, tried first the same day, was reverted after an independent review: a replayed Message took the task's current state. The writer fold was reviewed independently (no critical or high findings); each part is shown to fail with it disabled (mutation, 2026-10-23). Since 2026-10-23 (maintainer's decision) a turn that continues a stored task folds every Message, its first included: §3.1.2 gives the message-only stream to the exchange with "no task tracking", and §3.7 gives an agent's message on a task the role "Status Messages: Agents attach Messages to status update events". So a follow-up answered with a Message gets a task stream, and a SubscribeToTask stream on the task the same status update (§3.1.6, §3.5.2); reviewed independently. A follow-up answered with messages alone, setting no state, is re-parked in the interrupted state it waited in, with the last message as its status message (TerminalTracking::repark_if_silent; a second review found the task otherwise left Submitted, which the SDK's client read as an incomplete stream). Not covered, by design: a client that found a brand-new task's id (ListTasks) and subscribed before that task's first-event Message, which stays a direct reply as §3.1.2 allows, receives it bare; the spec has that exchange track no task.

entries.requirement: Message-only stream: If the agent returns a Message, the stream MUST contain exactly one `Message` object and then close immediately.
entries.notes: Exactly one Message, then the reader returns None; a read dropped while waiting for the first event keeps the decision (cancel-safety test).

entries.requirement: Task lifecycle stream: If the agent returns a Task, the stream MUST begin with the Task object, followed by zero or more TaskStatusUpdateEvent or TaskArtifactUpdateEvent objects.
entries.notes: A Message an executor writes once its task stream has begun (after a Task, status or artifact update) is sent, since 2026-10-23, as a TaskStatusUpdateEvent that keeps the state the turn last wrote (or, before any status, the state the turn began in) and carries the message in status.message. The writer folds it once, before the event takes its log position, so the send stream, a SubscribeToTask stream and a resumed replay carry one payload at that position (§3.5.2); the processors store it as a history entry and the status message, with no transition check, and push it. A fold in each stream's reader, tried first the same day, was reverted after an independent review: a replayed Message took the task's current state. The writer fold was reviewed independently (no critical or high findings); each part is shown to fail with it disabled (mutation, 2026-10-23). The send stream is therefore always a Task followed by status and artifact updates once the executor's first event is not a Message.

entries.requirement: The stream MUST close when the task reaches a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED).
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 a reader ends once it has delivered a terminal state (and whatever was queued ahead of it), instead of waiting for the executor to drop its writer; an executor still running, or writing, after its terminal status no longer holds the stream open. The conformance harness reads the raw channel so nothing_after_terminal still sees such writes. The test failed before the change (stream open after 5 s). A cancelled task reaches its terminal state on the queue whatever its executor's cancel hook writes (2026-10-13): only the default hook wrote Canceled there, so CancelTask against a hook overridden to release state stored Canceled while the send stream ended after Working with no terminal frame, and a halt or shutdown left such a task Working. After a hook that returns Ok without a terminal state the handler writes Canceled itself (TerminalTracking::cancel_with). Both tests failed before the change.

entries.requirement: The agent MAY return a `Task` for complex processing with status/artifact updates
entries.notes: Asserts a task-lifecycle stream starts with the Task snapshot then its updates; shown able to fail by disabling the provisional Task snapshot in InMemoryQueueReader::read (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: or MAY return a `Message` for direct streaming responses without task overhead.
entries.notes: A Message as the executor's first event is streamed as the whole response. Asserts a Message-answering agent streams exactly one Message and nothing else; shown able to fail by disabling the message-only branch in InMemoryQueueReader::read (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: The implementation MUST provide immediate feedback on progress and intermediate results.
entries.notes: The stream is returned before the executor finishes (the cooperative-executor test returns the stream while the executor waits on a Notify); events are broadcast as written. Disposition (audit register R33, approved 2026-10-14): a send stream's first frame waits for the executor's first event, with no time bound. Line 208 requires a message-only stream to contain exactly one Message, so a Task sent before the executor shows which kind of stream it is would break that MUST for an agent that answers with a Message; the executor's first event is the earliest the kind is known, so the wait ends there.

The operation MUST return only tasks visible to the authenticated client
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: met by the SDK, not left to the application. With an authenticating interceptor that identifies callers, caller isolation is the default (since 0.15): each caller's tasks are in a partition of their own, and ListTasks returns only that partition (Bob lists none of Alice's tasks). Without identities, or with share_tasks_across_callers(), tasks are visible tenant-wide by the deployer's choice. The earlier notes describing a default with no scoping were stale.

entries.requirement: SubscribeToTask TaskNotFoundError
UnsupportedOperationError: The operation is attempted on a task that is in a terminal state
The stream MUST terminate when the task reaches a terminal state
entries.notes: Every stream ends at the terminal event (in_memory.rs:1088-1097), and SubscribeToTask stays open across turns until one (STREAM-SUB-002, 2026-10-12). Since 2026-10-15 (maintainer decision) HandlerLimits::subscribe_max_idle is Option<Duration>, None by default, so a stream to a parked task no longer ends early at 300 s: it ends at the terminal state, when the task is deleted, or when the client goes, which every binding detects without the bound (SSE keep-alive write, WebSocket read loop and idle_timeout, gRPC tx.closed(), SLIMRPC session close; read 2026-10-15). An operator may still set a bound (with_subscribe_max_idle), which ends such a stream without a terminal state; that is a documented opt-out from this MUST, not the default. A store failure while waiting no longer ends the stream at the bound: it keeps polling and warns once per run of failures. A cancel whose executor hook writes nothing reaches the queue as Canceled (2026-10-13, see the 210 entry).

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return a `Task` object as the first event in the stream, representing the current state of the task at the time of subscription.
entries.notes: The Task is read at a known position (2026-10-13): the stream attaches to the queue first, at an exact position, and the task row is read once every event up to there is stored and none is being stored (streaming/event_queue/applied.rs), so the Task and the live events neither overlap nor leave a gap. Read before the attach, as until then, it trailed the broadcast and an event broadcast before the attach and stored after the read was in neither. The wait is bounded by subscribe_replay_catchup (2 s); past it the event log fills the gap after the Task. Outside the mark: a row CancelTask or another replica writes.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return all active push notification configurations for the specified task
and MAY support pagination for tasks with many configurations.
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 RequestHandler::on_list_push_configs_page pages the list on every binding (JSON-RPC and WebSocket params, HTTP+JSON and axum query, gRPC and SLIMRPC fields): ordered by id, at most pageSize, nextPageToken while more remain (base64url of the last id returned), InvalidField(pageToken) for one this server did not give, pageSize 0 read as unset. Without pageSize or pageToken the whole list is returned unordered, as before. Before: pageSize/pageToken were ignored and nextPageToken was always None; the list is bounded by max_push_configs_per_task either way. Existing tests assert 5 configs come back in 3 pages of at most 2 with no token on the last, also over JSON-RPC and REST; shown able to fail by making push_config_page.rs page() return every config unpaged (2026-10-20)
