entries.requirement: The operation MUST permanently remove the specified push notification configuration.
entries.notes: Delivery re-lists configs per event (push_delivery/mod.rs:72), so later events are not sent to a deleted webhook; no test asserts 'no notification after delete'. The next sentence, "No further notifications will be sent to the configured webhook after deletion", is tested by no_notification_reaches_a_webhook_after_its_config_is_deleted (2026-10-23, WP-C).

entries.requirement: This operation MUST be idempotent - multiple deletions of the same config have the same effect.
UnsupportedOperationError: The agent does not support authenticated extended cards
ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError: The agent declares support but does not have an extended agent card configured.
entries.notes: Returned when the handler's card declares the capability and no extended card is set with with_extended_agent_card (since 2026-10-14, audit register R68). Until then the public card was served in the extended card's place, and -32007 was returned only by a handler with no card at all, which now answers UnsupportedOperationError (see 3164).

entries.requirement: The client MUST authenticate the request using one of the schemes declared in the public AgentCard.securitySchemes and AgentCard.security fields.
entries.notes: Client: get_extended_agent_card does not check that credentials matching the card's schemes are attached; the caller must register an interceptor for one of them. For an APIKeySecurityScheme, AuthInterceptor::api_key sends the key in the header or cookie the scheme names, over JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and gRPC (e2e against ApiKeyAuthInterceptor); until 2026-10-14 the only API-key path wrote Authorization, which such an agent refuses. A key placed in the query string goes in the request URL over JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON (since 2026-10-14, audit register R67; refused before, as no transport could add a query parameter), and the gRPC and WebSocket transports refuse the call with ClientError::InvalidAuthScheme rather than send it without the key. Server side refuses the call unless an authenticating interceptor exists (or allow_unauthenticated_extended_card opt-out). Since 2026-10-20 a client built from a card checks every call (streaming included, on every transport) after its interceptors run, where the §13.4 plaintext check runs: the request must meet one of the card's securityRequirements, judged by where each declared scheme puts its credential (Authorization with the HTTP scheme, Bearer for OAuth2 and OIDC, the API key's header, query parameter or cookie; mutual TLS counts as met), so a credential the caller's own interceptor writes in a declared place passes and the 2026-10-18 objection holds only for one in a place the card does not declare; CredentialPreflight::Warn (default) logs once per client per mismatch kind, Refuse returns ClientError::InvalidAuthScheme before anything is sent, Off skips the check. Supplying the credential stays the caller's; refusing is opt-in (Refuse), the default warns. The SDK's part is placing a credential where a declared scheme says (AuthInterceptor::with_scheme, api_key; tested) and the server refusing GetExtendedAgentCard without one (tested); choosing the scheme is the caller's.

entries.requirement: The operation MAY return different details based on client authentication level, including additional skills, capabilities, or configuration not available in the public Agent Card.
entries.notes: RequestHandlerBuilder::with_extended_agent_card sets the card served to an authenticated caller, distinct from the public one. Without it a card that declares the capability answers ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError (since 2026-10-14; the public card used to be served). One extended card for every authenticated caller: no per-caller variation (see 3144). Until 2026-10-14 the builder had no extended-card setting, so the 'extended' card was always the public one (audit register R56). Existing test asserts two authenticated callers are served extended cards with different skills; shown able to fail by serving the configured extended card without the per-caller provider in extended_card.rs (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: Clients retrieving this extended card SHOULD replace their cached public Agent Card with the content received from this endpoint for the duration of their authenticated session or until the card's version changes.
entries.notes: The SDK caches a card in two places. A2aClient caches the capabilities it checks calls against (DeclaredCapabilities, from the card it was built from); since 2026-10-13 get_extended_agent_card replaces them with the extended card's (A2aClient::adopt_capabilities), keeping extendedAgentCard declared, and only when the client checks at all. Before, it kept the public card's, so a capability only the extended card declared was refused locally with CapabilityNotDeclared. The other, the resolver's, is replaced when the application calls CachingCardResolver::install_extended_card, which serves the extended card from resolve() until clear_extended_card() or invalidate(); the application decides when the session ends.

entries.requirement: Blocking (`return_immediately: false` or unset): The operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal state ... or an interrupted state ... before returning.
entries.notes: collect_events loops until `is_terminal() || is_interrupted()` (sync_collector.rs:242). Edge: if the executor returns without ever reaching a terminal/interrupted state, the collector drains (bounded by executor_drain_timeout) and answers with the non-terminal state (sync_collector.rs:205-221) -- an agent bug, but the SDK does not force a terminal state there.

entries.requirement: The response MUST include the latest task state with all artifacts and status information.
entries.notes: Artifacts are folded into the collected task and returned. Note the response omits `history` unless historyLength is set (respond.rs:36-48, decisions.rs:34), which the spec's 'implementation-defined default' for unset historyLength permits.

entries.requirement: Non-Blocking (`return_immediately: true`): The operation MUST return immediately after creating the task, even if processing is still in progress.
entries.notes: Returns the Submitted snapshot and spawns the background processor; test asserts state==Submitted and that the store later reaches Completed.

entries.requirement: historyLength 0: No history should be returned; the `history` field SHOULD be omitted
entries.notes: truncate_history returns None for n==0, so the field is omitted (not []) on GetTask, ListTasks and SendMessage responses.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST specify how service parameters are transmitted in their binding specification.
entries.notes: WebSocket: the binding specification (book/src/bindings/websocket.md §2) states the mechanism (upgrade headers, once per connection), the A2A-Version query fallback, value constraints, the reserved :path key, and that parameters cannot vary per request. SLIMRPC: slimrpc.md §3. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written. Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. The SDK authors the WebSocket binding, so the obligation is its own, met in its binding specification and pinned by the tests cited.

entries.requirement: A2A-Extensions: Comma-separated list of extension URIs that the client wants to use for the request (implied: server reads it as a service parameter; client can send it)
entries.notes: Server parses the lowercased `a2a-extensions` header/metadata on all bindings via build_call_context. Client, since 2026-10-13: ClientBuilder::with_extensions sends the URIs as one comma-separated header (gRPC metadata on gRPC) on every request an interceptor did not give the header, and WebSocketTransportConfig::with_extensions puts it on the upgrade, where the WebSocket server reads service parameters. extensions_e2e.rs checks what the executor sees on JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, gRPC and WebSocket, unary and streaming. Not tested over SLIMRPC. Until then a caller had to set the header itself.

entries.requirement: A2A-Version: ... If the version is not supported, the agent returns VersionNotSupportedError
entries.notes: Every binding, the axum adapter included (validate_a2a_request middleware), answers VersionNotSupportedError.

entries.requirement: As service parameter names MAY need to co-exist with other parameters ... all service parameters defined by this specification will be prefixed with `a2a-`.
entries.notes: Naming rule for the spec itself; SDK constants use the `A2A-` prefix. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: binds the specification project (its documents, website or process), not an implementation. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the two header constants' lines re-pointed (they cited doc-comment lines).

entries.requirement: Send Message operations MAY be idempotent. Agents may utilize the messageId to detect duplicate messages.
entries.notes: Implemented through an opt-in idempotency extension key in message metadata (IDEMPOTENCY_EXTENSION_URI), not by messageId alone. Asserts a retried send with the same idempotency key returns the first task and runs the agent once, and the key on another messageId is refused; shown able to fail by treating every key as absent in claim_send_key (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: A duplicate cancellation request MAY return `TaskNotFoundError` if the task has already been canceled and purged.
entries.notes: Purged task -> TaskNotFound (store miss). A duplicate cancel of a still-stored Canceled task returns TaskNotCancelableError (cancel_task.rs:48), consistent with that error's definition though not literally 'the same effect' as the first cancel. Asserts a duplicate cancel is TaskNotCancelable while the canceled task is stored and TaskNotFound once TTL eviction purges it; shown able to fail by disabling evict_expired (2026-10-20) The same line's "Cancel Task operations are idempotent - multiple cancellation requests have the same effect": a second cancel leaves the stored task as the first did and answers TaskNotCancelableError, which §3.1.5 lists for an already-canceled task (2026-10-23, WP-C).

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return appropriate errors
entries.notes: Every ServerError maps to an ErrorCode, HTTP status and gRPC code; covered by per-code unit tests.

entries.requirement: Servers ... SHOULD provide actionable information to help clients resolve issues.
entries.notes: Refusals name the parameter and the accepted form or limit; the wire test pins six (message.id empty and too long, no parts, metadata over the size limit and not an object, unsupported A2A-Version). Shown to fail with the message.id label changed.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST reject requests with invalid or missing authentication credentials
entries.notes: The bundled ApiKey/Bearer/JWT interceptors refuse a missing or invalid credential with 401/UNAUTHENTICATED on every binding. Since 2026-10-18 build() refuses a card whose securityRequirements (top-level or a skill's, with no empty {} requirement making it optional) ask for a credential when no interceptor authenticates, unless authenticated_upstream() says a gateway in front checks it; so a handler can no longer serve a secured card unauthenticated by omission. tests/auth_every_method.rs calls every method in Method::ALL on JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON with no credential and a wrong one and requires 401 each time, with the valid token as the control (the official TCK has no test for this, findings §16 AUTH-SERVER-002). Since 2026-10-20 that holds for a malformed request too: every binding read a request's params before the chain ran (JSON-RPC until that morning, HTTP+JSON, gRPC and WebSocket until the afternoon), and ListTasks checked pageSize and statusTimestampAfter, and CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig its taskId, before admission, so a caller with no credential got 400 / INVALID_ARGUMENT / -32602 naming the field where a well-formed request got the refusal. A request whose params cannot be read is now admitted first (RequestHandler::admit_unreadable) and the handler checks run after admission; the binding's version check, the body's size cap and read timeout, and routing still come first, since they refuse a well-formed request alike. The auth_before_params tests send each malformed request on every binding with no credential, a wrong one and the right one.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD include authentication challenge information in the error response
entries.notes: WWW-Authenticate added on HTTP bindings for 401. Since 2026-10-13 gRPC sends the same challenge as `www-authenticate` metadata on UNAUTHENTICATED, and SLIMRPC, whose errors carry no metadata, ends the message with `(WWW-Authenticate: <challenge>)`; both had dropped it. WebSocket refuses a credential per message with -32600 carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo whose metadata holds the challenge as `www-authenticate` (refusal_detail; websocket_binding_spec.rs a_refused_credential_carries_the_refusal_detail) (corrected 2026-10-23: the note said WebSocket sent no challenge).

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD specify which authentication scheme is required
entries.notes: Challenge carries the scheme (e.g. `Bearer realm="a2a"`), on HTTP as a header, on gRPC as metadata and on SLIMRPC in the message (since 2026-10-13 for the last two).

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return an authorization error when the authenticated client lacks required permissions
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: A2aError::permission_denied and insufficient_scope answer 403 / PERMISSION_DENIED on every binding, and the SDK now applies a permission itself: JwtValidator::require_scope refuses a valid token lacking a required scope with 403 (not 401), on both HTTP bindings in the test. Which permissions an operation needs beyond that is the agent's policy, expressed in an interceptor.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD indicate what permission or scope is missing (without leaking sensitive information ...)
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: A2aError::insufficient_scope(message, scopes) carries the RFC 6750 §3 challenge Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="...", which every binding sends with its 403 (header, gRPC metadata, WebSocket ErrorInfo metadata). JwtValidator::require_scope names only the scopes the token lacks, and only to a caller whose token verified, so a caller without a valid credential learns nothing about them (the test's forged token gets 401 with no scope in the challenge).

entries.requirement: Servers MUST NOT reveal the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: another caller's task answers exactly as an unknown id does (TaskNotFound, the test's control), from Get, Cancel, Subscribe and a continuing SendMessage, and their configs likewise; ACTS SEC-AUTH-003 and CORE-ERR-009 pass on three bindings. Since 2026-10-18 an unauthenticated push-config call is also refused for its credential before the capability check, so it learns nothing about the agent either.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST validate all input parameters before processing
entries.notes: validate_send_params runs before any side effect (ids, parts, input modes, metadata shape/size). Since 2026-10-13 also a message's referenceTaskIds (validate_id, as its taskId) and ListTasks' pageSize, which must be 1 to 100 (a2a.proto); both were accepted unchecked, the page size clamped to 1000 and 0 read as 50.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD specify which parameter(s) failed validation and why
entries.notes: Each handler validation message names the parameter (message.id, message, request metadata, A2A version); body-shape errors also carry a google.rpc.BadRequest field violation (jsonrpc_error_details.rs). The handler's own validation errors name the field in text only, not as a BadRequest detail: ServerError::InvalidParams carries a String, and changing it would break callers that match it.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD provide guidance on valid parameter values or formats
entries.notes: Messages state the limit or accepted value ("got 5000, max ...", "max 1048576", "must be a JSON object", "this server supports 1.0"); pinned by the wire test.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return a not found error when a requested resource does not exist or is not accessible to the authenticated client
entries.notes: TaskNotFound (404/NOT_FOUND/-32001) for missing tasks and push configs on every binding.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD NOT distinguish between "does not exist" and "not authorized"
entries.notes: Tenant-scoped store returns None for another tenant's task, which surfaces as the same TaskNotFound.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD return appropriate error codes for temporary failures vs. permanent errors
entries.notes: Overloaded -> 503 with an AIP-193 status of RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED); Halted -> 503 / UNAVAILABLE; a rate-limit refusal -> 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; internal -> 500 / INTERNAL. Until 2026-10-10 an overload's REST body read status INTERNAL under 503, naming a permanent failure. Since 2026-10-14 (audit register R57) a SQL store whose database cannot answer for now (pool timed out or closed, I/O, SQLite BUSY or LOCKED, Postgres connection, serialization, deadlock, lock, resource and shutdown codes) answers A2aError::unavailable: 503 / UNAVAILABLE, gRPC and SLIMRPC UNAVAILABLE; every database error was 500 / INTERNAL. A send and a push config's creation keep 500 / INTERNAL, since this SDK's client re-sends those on 503 as refused before processing.

entries.requirement: Servers MAY include retry guidance (e.g., Retry-After header in HTTP)
entries.notes: A rate-limit refusal carries Retry-After (whole seconds to the end of the window) on HTTP+JSON and a RetryInfo detail on the JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, WebSocket and gRPC bindings. The SLIMRPC binding (bindings/a2a-protocol-slimrpc, error.rs) answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED without the delay: SLIMRPC errors have no details field. Overload (503) and halt (503) send no retry guidance: neither has a known end.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD log system errors for diagnostic purposes
entries.notes: Failures are recorded on the RPC span (error.type, otel.status_code=ERROR) and in metrics.on_error, and trace_error! logs a system error as an ERROR event at 19 call sites: executor failures and panics, failed task-store and queue writes, JSON-RPC and REST response serialization, failed audit writes, and a too-short HS256 secret. Since 2026-10-12 a test asserts the executor-failure event: an executor returning an internal error is logged at ERROR with the task id and the cause (three hand mutants killed: the call deleted, demoted to WARN, the cause dropped). The other sites use the same macro and are not tested one by one. Behind the `tracing` feature, on by default. Before: no test asserted that an internal error is logged.

entries.requirement: All error responses ... MUST convey ... Error Code ... Error Message
entries.notes: JSON-RPC {code,message,data}, REST AIP-193 {code,status,message,details}, gRPC Status(code,message,details).

entries.requirement: Each object in the [details] array MUST include a `@type` key
entries.notes: Every detail carries @type. An A2A error's ErrorInfo (and RetryInfo for a rate limit) comes from error_info_data. A2aError.data follows it as a typed detail (sse::error_details, used by JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and WebSocket): as it is when it names its own string @type (a google.rpc.BadRequest), otherwise as a google.protobuf.Struct in the ProtoJSON Any form, {"@type": ..., "value": {...}}, with a non-object under value (since 2026-10-14, audit register R19; the fields were written beside @type, the form a2a-go writes, which a ProtoJSON Any decoder rejects). The gRPC binding sends the same data as BadRequest field violations or a Struct Any (dispatch/grpc/details.rs).

entries.requirement: Well-known types from the google.rpc error model (e.g., ErrorInfo, BadRequest) SHOULD be used where applicable
entries.notes: ErrorInfo on every A2A-specific error. Since ef31df9 a body or params that do not deserialize carry google.rpc.BadRequest with the field path (jsonrpc_error_details.rs, bad_request_details.rs). Since 2026-10-14 (audit register, the §3.3.2 row) the handler's own request checks carry a BadRequest naming the field too, through the new ServerError::InvalidField: ids (empty, too long, reference_task_ids), message.role, message.parts, every metadata and number-range check, a part's raw, the push config's required ids, taskId, url, authentication.scheme, token and credentials, ListTasks pageSize and statusTimestampAfter, and the REST query parameters. They named the field in the message only. Errors that name no single field (a per-task config limit, a card refused at build()) stay InvalidParams.

entries.requirement: Protocol bindings MUST map these elements to their native error representations while preserving semantic meaning
entries.notes: Per-code mappings to HTTP status and gRPC code are unit tested.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to enable multi-turn interactions
entries.notes: Non-terminal continuations reuse the task id; a send to a task whose executor is still running is refused (UnsupportedOperation), see tests.rs concurrent_send_to_in_flight_task_is_rejected. A continuation sent as soon as the task parks is built from the task as the previous turn left it (2026-10-13): it waits for that turn to store its events and reads the task again, where it used to save over what the turn had just stored, such as an artifact. Asserts a follow-up to an input-required task runs as the same task, completes it, and both user messages are in its history; shown able to fail by refusing non-terminal continuations in resolve_task_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: When clients attempt to use operations or features that require capabilities not declared ... the agent MUST return an appropriate error response
entries.notes: Summary of 573-576 below, each TESTED. The checks are skipped only for a handler built with RequestHandlerBuilder::without_agent_card(), an explicit statement that it is not a public A2A server or that its card is published elsewhere; since 2026-10-12 build() refuses a handler with no card otherwise (spec §8.1). Before: every check was skipped whenever no card was configured, which was the default.

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications is false or not present, push notification config operations (Create, Get, List, Delete) MUST return PushNotificationNotSupportedError
entries.notes: All four ops refuse when the card does not declare pushNotifications, and when no push sender is wired. build() refuses a card that declares pushNotifications with no sender, so a served card never advertises operations that refuse. Until 2026-10-13 only Create checked the sender and such a card was served.

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.streaming is false or not present, SendStreamingMessage or SubscribeToTask MUST return UnsupportedOperationError
entries.notes: ensure_streaming_supported refuses SendStreamingMessage and SubscribeToTask unless capabilities.streaming is true. Tested over JSON-RPC for streaming false and absent (code -32004 on both methods, against an existing task); shown to fail with the check disabled. A no-op only for a handler built without_agent_card(); build() otherwise requires a card (2026-10-12).

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, Get Extended Agent Card MUST return UnsupportedOperationError. If the agent declares support but has not configured an extended card, it MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError.
entries.notes: The handler's card decides: not declared, UnsupportedOperation; declared, the extended card if one is set, else ExtendedAgentCardNotConfigured (since 2026-10-14; the public card was served); no card at all, the extended card if one is set, else UnsupportedOperation (since 2026-10-14; it was NotConfigured).

entries.requirement: When a server requests use of an extension marked as `required: true` ... but the client does not declare support for it, the agent MUST return ExtensionSupportRequiredError
entries.notes: Every operation now refuses a client that does not declare a required extension; GetExtendedAgentCard was the one that skipped it.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD validate capability support by examining the Agent Card before attempting operations that require optional capabilities
entries.notes: A client built from a card refuses, before sending, every call that needs an optional capability the card does not set to true: streaming and resubscription (streaming), the four push-config methods and a send carrying an inline push config (pushNotifications), GetExtendedAgentCard (extendedAgentCard). The refusal is ClientError::CapabilityNotDeclared; nothing reaches the transport (tested against a recording transport for all ten call shapes). ClientBuilder::without_capability_checks and the CLI's --no-capability-check opt out; a client built from a bare URL has no card and checks nothing. Required extensions are not checked client-side: the client cannot know which it supports.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY generate a new contextId when processing a Message that does not include a contextId field
entries.notes: UUIDv4 generated. Asserts a message without contextId gets a non-empty contextId, distinct per message, which the agent runs in; shown able to fail by generating a constant contextId in resolve_context_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: If an agent generates a new contextId, it MUST be included in the response (either Task or Message)
entries.notes: Task responses always carry context_id. A direct Message reply whose contextId the executor left empty now gets the task's contextId, on the blocking path and on a message-only stream; a contextId the executor set is kept. Until 2026-10-10 such a reply named no context.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY accept and preserve client-provided contextId values
entries.notes: Client contextId used verbatim after validation. Asserts a client contextId is kept verbatim on the response, the stored task and the agent request context; shown able to fail by replacing client contextIds with generated ones in resolve_context_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: If an agent cannot accept a client-provided contextId, it MUST reject the request with an error and MUST NOT generate a new contextId for the response
entries.notes: Invalid contextId -> InvalidParams before any task is created; a provided contextId is never replaced.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD NOT provide a client-generated contextId to a server unless they understand how the server will process that contextId
entries.notes: The client SDK never fills context_id itself; the caller builds the Message. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: whether to send a contextId of its own is a decision about the client's conversation, which only the caller can make; the SDK never generates one. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the citation named a blank line; it now names where the caller's params are serialized unchanged.

entries.requirement: Server-generated contextId values SHOULD be treated as opaque identifiers by clients
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client keeps a server's contextId as the opaque ContextId newtype and never parses or derives anything from it. Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. The SDK's client is a client: it keeps the server's contextId as an opaque newtype, and the test added the same day shows a value with separators, escapes, non-ASCII and padding reaching the caller byte for byte.

entries.requirement: All tasks and messages with the same contextId SHOULD be treated as part of the same conversational session
entries.notes: SDK groups by context (find_task_by_context, per-context lock) and passes context_id to the executor; conversational semantics are the agent's. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the SDK keys storage, locks and continuation on contextId and gives the executor the context's latest task (RequestContext::stored_task); what a conversational session means is the agent's. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): multi_turn_same_context_id asserted only that both sends succeed; the context_lookup_tests that pin the grouping replace it. Re-audited 2026-10-24: the executor sees one task for the context, the most recently updated non-terminal one among the ten most recent, else the most recent (find_task_by_context); a task forked in a context starts with clean history and artifacts. The cited tests pin that lookup, not 'the same conversational session', which no test could.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY use the contextId to maintain internal state, conversational history, or LLM context
entries.notes: context_id exposed on RequestContext. Asserts an agent keying a turn counter on RequestContext.context_id sees turns accumulate per context (1, 2 in A; 1 in B; 3 in A); shown able to fail by ignoring client contextIds in resolve_context_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement context expiration or cleanup policies
entries.notes: Task-store TTL/capacity and retention modules. Asserts that with a task TTL a finished context is listed before expiry and gone after, while a context with an open task is kept; shown able to fail by disabling evict_expired (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: [Agents] SHOULD document any such policies
entries.notes: Deployment-specific; SDK documents its own TTL/capacity knobs in rustdoc. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the SDK documents its own defaults (TaskStoreConfig: task_ttl, max_capacity; book deployment pages), but which policy a deployment runs, and where it tells its users, is the deployer's.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST generate a unique taskId for each new task they create
entries.notes: UUIDv4 per new task; test asserts a new id on a new round in the same context.

entries.requirement: The generated taskId MUST be included in the Task object returned to the client
entries.notes: Task.id is a required field; tests read task.id from the response and fetch it from the store.

entries.requirement: When a client includes a taskId in a Message, it MUST reference an existing task
entries.notes: Client-side obligation; the server enforces it (line 614). Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: which task a client means is the caller's knowledge; the server side of the same rule (TaskNotFound for an unknown taskId, §3.4.2 line 614) is TESTED. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the citation named a blank line; it now names where the caller's params are serialized unchanged.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST return a TaskNotFoundError if the provided taskId does not correspond to an existing task
Clients MAY include the contextId in subsequent messages
entries.notes: Message.context_id field exposed. Asserts a client message carrying back the server-generated contextId serialises it as contextId and lands in that context; shown able to fail by ignoring client contextIds in resolve_context_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: Clients MAY use taskId (with or without contextId) to continue or refine a specific task
entries.notes: A refused continuation leaves the task it names as it was: an inline push config is registered before the turn touches the row, and a refusal no longer runs the new-task rollback that deleted the row (2026-10-13). When the config is accepted but the turn cannot be saved, a config the server created is withdrawn; one the request named by id stays, since it may have replaced the client's own. Asserts a taskId-only follow-up continues that task in its inferred context, and taskId plus contextId does too; shown able to fail by not inferring the context from the task in resolve_context_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: Clients MAY use contextId without taskId to start a new task within an existing conversation context
entries.notes: Asserts contextId without taskId creates a new task in that context and leaves the open earlier task input-required; shown able to fail by making such a send reuse the open task in resolve_task_id (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: Agents MUST infer contextId from the task if only taskId is provided
Agents MUST reject messages containing mismatching contextId and taskId
entries.notes: Rejected with InvalidParams.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use the referenceTaskIds field in Message to explicitly reference related tasks
entries.notes: Field exposed on Message; client SDK never sets it. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: which tasks are related is the caller's knowledge; Message::with_reference_task_ids (message.rs:223) sets the field, and the server resolves it since 2026-10-18 (RequestContext::referenced_tasks). Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the citation named the licence header.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-18 the handler resolves message.referenceTaskIds into RequestContext::referenced_tasks before the executor runs: read in the caller's partition (another caller's task resolves to nothing, as GetTask does), unknown ids skipped, duplicates once, at most 16. Using them is the agent's. Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. The requirement binds the agent's reasoning; the SDK's hook (RequestContext::referenced_tasks, resolved in the caller's partition) is tested.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD leverage the shared contextId to provide contextually relevant responses
entries.notes: The handler gives the executor the latest task stored for the message's contextId as RequestContext::stored_task, with its history, on every send that names a context; using it for relevance is the agent's. Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. The requirement binds the agent's reasoning; the SDK's hook is RequestContext::stored_task for the message's contextId. Re-audited 2026-10-24: the lookup behind it is pinned by context_lookup_tests; no test asserts that a new task (no taskId) in an existing context reaches the executor with the prior task as stored_task.

entries.requirement: All implementations MUST deliver events in the order they were generated. Events MUST NOT be reordered during transmission
entries.notes: One broadcast channel per task, and writes to it take turns from the moment a position is assigned until the event is broadcast (2026-10-13), so writes in flight at once (CancelTask's beside the executor's, a terminal event held for the store's verdict) reach the persistence channel and every stream in position order. Until then a later write could overtake a held terminal event, and on a multi-threaded runtime any two writes could swap. The SSE, gRPC and WebSocket writers forward each stream sequentially.

entries.requirement: An agent MAY serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task
entries.notes: Asserts two SubscribeToTask streams opened beside the originating stream all see the task through to Completed; shown able to fail by refusing a subscribe while the task has a live queue (a dead broadcast receiver alone does not fail it: the store-backed reattach hook still delivers the terminal status) (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: Events MUST be broadcast to all active streams for that task
Each stream MUST receive the same events in the same order
entries.notes: A stream that falls behind the bounded broadcast buffer now catches up from the task's event log, after the last position it delivered, and goes on live (2026-10-12), so a slow stream receives the same events in the same order as a fast one. Only a complete replay whose head is still in the log is used, and a live event that does not follow it is reported as a lag, so no stream skips an event silently. Since 2026-10-15 (maintainer decision) a replay longer than subscribe_replay_limit is read a page at a time, for a lag, a missed turn and a Last-Event-ID resume, and the stream reads the channel again only once the last page is in; before, a lag past the limit ended with streamLagged, and a resume past it skipped the positions between the replay's end and the live receiver's start with no streamLagged at all (event_log_tests pinned [snapshot, 1, 2] for a log of five). A page with a hole, an empty page, or a read cut short by the catch-up deadline never asks for more (log_replay_tests). After an independent review (2026-10-15): a resume whose first read the log had not caught up with skipped the rest silently, and now reads on while the log moves forward, reporting what it cannot supply; the hook answers a gap-free page the log covers even when it trails the writer, rather than nothing; a page the log cannot supply after a lag is reported once. Remaining, why PARTIAL/low, each ending the stream with an explicit streamLagged after what was delivered: a lag beyond what the log still holds (the in-memory stores keep 512 events per task by default; the SQL stores keep the whole log, so with them this case cannot arise short of a failed append), or a custom store without an event log. Every stream receives positions in the order they were assigned, because writes are broadcast in that order (2026-10-13, see spec line 683); before that a reader, which skips a position it has passed, could lose an event another write had overtaken. A SubscribeToTask stream across turns replays from the log what each reattach answer leaves it owing (2026-10-13): the events a turn broadcast before the reattach hook found its queue, a turn that ran between two polls and parked again or finished, and, on a replica sharing the store, the running replica's events, a poll late. Until then all of them were lost without a streamLagged. Without a log the turn's missed events are reported as streamLagged, and a turn numbered from 1 is no longer skipped as already delivered. A read dropped while the log is read keeps the replay owed, for a lag too. Since 2026-10-15 (audit register R69) a subscription with no local queue reads the task with the event-log position it reflects, in one store read (TaskStore::get_with_position), and replays the log after that position. It read the log's end and then the task: another replica's processor logs each event before it stores it, so an event logged before the first read and stored after the second was in neither the snapshot nor the replay and was lost with no streamLagged (reproduced by a test that fails on the old order), and one logged and stored between them arrived twice. Every shipped store records the position atomically with each write the processors make inside AppliedPosition::scope; a custom store that reports none falls back to the old order, which can still lose that one event. A turn after a failed append is numbered after the later of the log's end and the stored position, so its first event no longer takes the failed event's position and is not skipped as already delivered by a subscriber past it (found by an independent review of R69, 2026-10-15; the live-subscriber case predates R69). During a rolling upgrade a replica on an earlier release does not write the position, so a subscriber can receive events twice until every replica is upgraded. A continuation sent the moment a task parks no longer numbers its events over the previous turn's (2026-10-13): it was admitted when the executor returned, before the processor had logged the turn's last events, so its positions collided and its events were dropped from the log. A turn's queue is now released once its events are stored; within one process only. A replay with a position missing, which a failed append leaves, is not used either (2026-10-13): a lag across it is reported as streamLagged and a resume across it starts from the snapshot, where the stream used to skip the lost event silently. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept PARTIAL/low: a stream that lags beyond what the in-memory log retains (512 events per task by default) ends with streamLagged after what was delivered, so it does not receive every event; the SQL stores keep the whole log. Closing it would take an unbounded in-memory log, which the store cap exists to prevent. Re-examined 2026-10-20: the 512 is TaskStoreConfig::max_events_per_task's default (DEFAULT_MAX_EVENTS_PER_TASK, store/task_store/config.rs) and None removes the bound, and the SQL stores keep the whole log, so a deployment can meet the MUST today by configuration; what stays short of it is the bounded in-memory default, which trades the guarantee for memory. The engineering alternative weighed: trim the in-memory log only below the lowest position an attached stream still owes (a per-task watermark), so a lagging stream loses nothing while memory stays bounded by the slowest attached reader up to a hard ceiling; past the ceiling the stream would still end with streamLagged. It changes the store/stream contract the 2026-10-15 decisions settled, so it was the maintainer's call; the maintainer decided on 2026-10-20 to build it. Since 2026-10-20 (maintainer decision) an attached stream holds the positions it still owes in the in-memory log (EventHolds, TaskStore::hold_events, synchronous, default None), taken when the stream is built, inside the request's tenant scope, at the first position it may read from the log (a resume's Last-Event-ID, or a late snapshot's position, when lower; a subscription holds the log from the resume position, or from the start, while its snapshot waits for the store), raised after each read to the lowest position it may still read (a paged resume's page end, not the live receiver's start), never lowered (a fresh-numbered queue's reset to 0 pins nothing: its positions are in no log), kept across turns while the reattach hook and the log are awaited, and released when the stream ends or is dropped. The bound (max_events_per_task, 512) drops an event only once no hold owes it, up to a ceiling of max_held_events_factor times the bound (default 8, so 4,096 events; None is no ceiling; Some(1) is the old behaviour); past the ceiling the oldest is dropped anyway and reported (event_append_error::HOLD_CEILING). The audit, encrypted and tenant-aware wrappers forward it, the tenant store to the request's partition. A stream lagging 62 positions behind a bound of 10 now receives every one (stream_lag_holds; the same configuration ended with streamLagged before, which stream_lag_catch_up pinned). Kept PARTIAL/low: a stream lagging past the ceiling still ends with streamLagged after what it delivered, which the ceiling exists to allow (an unbounded hold would let a client that stops reading pin its task's log for as long as its connection lasts); so does a lag on a custom store that keeps a bounded log without holds. Independent review (2026-10-20), two defects fixed the same day: a streaming send took its hold only after the event processor had started appending and a historyLength store read had been awaited, so a stream that lagged in that window still ended with streamLagged (tests/stream_hold_before_append.rs the_send_stream_holds_the_log_before_its_history_is_read, which fails with the old order: 0 of 60 artifacts, streamLagged 58); and a finished task kept its held log, up to the ceiling, until it expired, since only an append trimmed it (now the eviction sweep trims a released held log to the bound: hold_tests the_eviction_sweep_trims_a_released_held_log_to_the_bound). Some(1) now consults no hold and reports nothing, the old trim exactly; the ceiling is logged once per task. The subscription's setup hold (subscribe/hold.rs) is pinned since 2026-10-24 (gap_tests the_log_is_held_while_the_snapshot_waits_for_the_store, which fails with the hold disabled and no other test does): the in-memory processor logs and then stores each event in order, so the log runs at most one event ahead of the snapshot the subscription reads and the window the hold guards cannot open past the bound with this store; the test appends to the log by hand during the snapshot's wait, as a store whose log can run further ahead would. Since 2026-10-24 (the independent review of 2026-10-20, finding 6) replay_after reports whether it queued a replay, and when the snapshot the store could not bring up to the queue lacks positions (the replay was owed to cover them) and no replay came (a store without a log, an unreadable log, a log with a hole, a log that no longer reaches back), the stream yields the snapshot and then streamLagged counting the positions between, where it used to go on live and skip them with no streamLagged (gap_tests, four tests, which fail with the report disabled; a whole log and a whole snapshot report nothing, pinned by the other two). Since 2026-10-20 a continuation's save records the event-log position of the task it was built from: the read the queue lease makes to number the turn (handler/messaging/basis.rs, admission::resume_after), whose artifacts and metadata the save now carries. The save replaces the stored artifacts and metadata, so an event another replica's still-running turn folded after that read is gone from the task; the save was unscoped and kept the position that fold had stored, so a subscription on a replica with no live queue started from a task lacking the event at a position past it, and the event was in neither its snapshot nor its replay, with no streamLagged (tests/stale_write_position, which fails on the old code with the task stored at position 3 without the artifact logged at 3, on the in-memory store shared by two handlers, on SQLite and on PostgreSQL). Every shipped store stores a scoped position even when it is lower than the stored one (applied_position). The new turn is numbered after the position recorded, so the lower position can give two events one position only where concurrent turns on two replicas already can (single-writer admission does not cross replicas, tests/multi_replica.rs). Still open: the task itself keeps the lost update, and the continuing turn's first fold stores a position past it again, so a subscriber starting after that fold still misses it; only a compare-and-set write would refuse the stale save. A cancel's status-only write leaves a terminal task, which no subscription starts from.

entries.requirement: Closing one stream MUST NOT affect other active streams for the same task
entries.notes: Readers are independent broadcast::Receivers and nothing cancels a task when a stream closes. The test drops the originating SendStreamingMessage stream and checks a SubscribeToTask stream still reaches the terminal event. Not injection-proven: no single-point code fault produces the violation today; the test guards against adding one (e.g. cancel-on-disconnect).

entries.requirement: Patch version numbers SHOULD NOT be used in requests, responses and Agent Cards
entries.notes: A2A_VERSION = "1.0" used for headers and card builder; some test fixtures use "1.0.0" but no production path does.

entries.requirement: [Patch version numbers] MUST not be considered when clients and servers negotiate protocol versions
entries.notes: Neither side compares the patch. The server accepts a request whose A2A-Version names its Major.Minor, whatever follows (is_served_version). The client keeps the card's interfaces of protocol major 1 (is_compatible: "1.0.0" and "1.1-rc1" both count) in card order and sends 1.0, so it does not compare the minor either: a 1.1 interface listed first is chosen and addressed as 1.0.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST send the A2A-Version header with each request
entries.notes: All four transports set it; JSON-RPC/REST covered implicitly by e2e tests against the default (version-required) RestDispatcher/JsonRpcDispatcher. WebSocket sends it on the upgrade only (per connection). The agent card fetch sends it too since 2026-10-13 (it went without), unless the caller passes its own A2A-Version in CardFetchOptions. SLIMRPC sends it as the a2a-version metadata key. Its multicast client (SlimRpcMulticast) sent none until 2026-10-13, hidden by the SLIMRPC server accepting a missing version; the multicast tests now run against a server that requires it.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY provide the A2A-Version as a request parameter instead of a header.
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-15, opt-in: VersionQueryInterceptor adds A2A-Version=1.0 to every request's query parameters, which the JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON transports append to the URL; the header is still sent beside it, so a server reading both (this SDK's, dispatch/version.rs requested_version: header first, then the parameter) answers the same either way, and a proxy that drops unknown headers no longer drops the version. Sending the parameter instead of the header was not chosen: a server that reads only the header would take the request for 0.3. gRPC and WebSocket have no per-request query string and send the version as metadata. Existing tests assert the server honours and validates ?A2A-Version= without the header and the client interceptor puts A2A-Version=1.0 on the URL; shown able to fail by dropping the query fallback in requested_version and by never adding the parameter in VersionQueryInterceptor (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: (implied) Server must honour A2A-Version supplied as a request parameter (`?A2A-Version=1.0`), since clients MAY send it that way and agents MUST process the requested version
entries.notes: dispatch::requested_version reads the header, else the ?A2A-Version= parameter, on JSON-RPC, REST, the WebSocket upgrade and axum.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST process requests using the semantics of the requested A2A-Version (matching Major.Minor).
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 (maintainer decision) a request is served only when its A2A-Version names this server's Major.Minor, 1.0, with any patch; any other version, 1.1 included, is VersionNotSupportedError naming 1.0, on every binding through one validator (the WebSocket handshake had its own copy). Until then any 1.x was accepted and served with 1.0 semantics, as the official Python SDK still does (_is_version_compatible compares the major only).

entries.requirement: If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a VersionNotSupportedError.
entries.notes: The axum adapter now validates A2A-Version like the other bindings.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST interpret empty value as 0.3 version.
entries.notes: Empty means 0.3 and is refused by default on every binding: JSON-RPC, REST, axum, WebSocket, gRPC and, since 2026-10-13, SLIMRPC, which until then served it as 1.0. Only the explicit opt-outs (accept_missing_version_header, gRPC with_require_version_header(false), SLIMRPC with_require_version(false)) serve it as 1.0; a server so configured is not conforming here, by the deployer's choice. PARTIAL until 2026-10-13: this note said every binding refused while SLIMRPC did not.

entries.requirement: Tooling libraries and SDKs ... MUST provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning, such as negotiation of the transport and protocol version used.
entries.notes: ClientBuilder::from_card filters interfaces by protocol major then binding preference; server exposes validate_version_metadata for out-of-tree bindings.

entries.requirement: Messages SHOULD NOT be used to deliver task outputs.
entries.notes: Agent's choice; SDK provides TaskUpdater-style artifact() helper. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: §3.1.1 allows a direct Message reply, so the SDK cannot tell output from communication; EventEmitter::artifact is the path it offers.

entries.requirement: Results SHOULD BE returned using Artifacts associated with a Task.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: as the SHOULD NOT on the same line; artifacts are what EventEmitter::artifact writes.

entries.requirement: Clients using streaming ... MAY not receive all status update messages if the client is disconnected and then reconnects.
entries.notes: Informative allowance; SDK additionally offers SSE resumption (sse_resumption_e2e.rs) which narrows the gap. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: an allowance describing what a client may experience, not something an implementation does.

entries.requirement: Messages MUST NOT be considered a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information.
entries.notes: Design guidance for agent/client authors; not testable in the SDK. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: a design rule for agent and client authors; the SDK's own critical signals do not depend on message delivery: the failure class and an approval request ride in the metadata of the task's status message, which is stored as Task.status.message and returned by GetTask; provenance rides on Message and Artifact metadata (failure.rs, approval.rs, provenance.rs). Corrected 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the note said Task.status and task metadata, and none of them uses Task.metadata. Re-audited 2026-10-24: what makes the SDK's critical signals defensible is that they are Task state re-readable by GetTask (TaskStatus.message), not that they avoid Messages: 'do not depend on stream delivery'. The delegation helper reads the failure class from the streamed terminal status and, on a broken stream, reports Outcome::Lost without re-reading it with GetTask, so the class is lost with the stream; safe degradation, not a violation.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY choose to persist all Messages that contain important information in the Task history
entries.notes: SDK persists every agent Message event into Task.history (capped at 1024). Asserts an agent Message emitted mid-task is stored in Task.history after the user message on both the blocking and streaming paths; shown able to fail by removing history.push(msg) in sync_collector.rs and in background/state_machine.rs respectively (2026-10-20)

entries.requirement: clients MUST NOT rely on this behavior unless negotiated out-of-band.
entries.notes: Client-author obligation. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: an obligation on client authors; the SDK client reads task state from Task and status events, not from message history.

entries.requirement: All protocol bindings MUST provide functionally equivalent representations of these data structures.
test_evidence: crates/a2a-protocol-types/tests/proptest_proto_convert.rs:233 task_wire_roundtrip (proptest domain->prost bytes->domain round trip; the block holds one such property per type)
entries.notes: One domain model (serde JSON) with a prost conversion layer for gRPC; golden fixtures from the official Python SDK prove JSON<->proto equivalence. What a client sends is checked since 2026-10-13 (make_portable): a raw part must be base64, read as the gRPC conversion reads it and kept in standard padded form; an integer beyond ±2^53 in metadata or a data part, which the gRPC conversion refuses, is InvalidParams. Before, any such value was stored, and the task could not be read over gRPC (GetTask, ListTasks pages with it and SubscribeToTask answered INTERNAL). An executor's events are held to the same rules at the queue writer since 2026-10-14 (content.rs make_portable, audit register R64), in every event kind and in a task snapshot's status, artifacts and history: a raw part that is not base64, an integer beyond ±2^53, or a metadata that is not a JSON object (all a google.protobuf.Struct holds) is InvalidParams before the event is persisted or broadcast, and raw is kept in standard padded form. Before, such an artifact was served over JSON and failed a gRPC read. A task store written before the check can still hold one; the gRPC stream then ends at it (dispatch/grpc/native.rs reader_to_native_stream_stops_after_a_conversion_error).

entries.requirement: The agent MUST include authentication credentials in the request headers as specified in the PushNotificationConfig.authentication field.
entries.notes: The sender writes Authorization for Bearer and Basic (case-insensitive), as a2a-go v2.5.0 does. A config naming any other scheme is now refused at creation with InvalidParams, so no webhook is called without the credentials its config specifies. Until 2026-10-10 such a config was stored and delivered without credentials (a2a-go still does that). The sender's runtime drop remains for configs stored before. Since 2026-10-13 a token or credentials a header cannot carry (CR, LF or another control character) is InvalidParams at creation, inline or by CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig; it was stored and refused at every delivery. v1.0.1's text names PushNotificationConfig, which the v1.0.1 proto does not define: the message with `authentication` is TaskPushNotificationConfig (a2a.proto line 469), the name upstream main uses since. Since 2026-10-18 a config whose authentication carries no credentials (absent, empty or whitespace) is refused at creation, naming authentication.credentials: it could only ever be delivered without them. A config stored before that sends no Authorization rather than an empty Bearer prefix.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. WebhookOutcome::status() is 200 for Accepted and for Duplicate (a retry the agent sent after a lost acknowledgement is acknowledged, not re-processed), and 4xx only for a refusal; the end-to-end test drives the server's HttpPushSender against it.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. Duplicate detection is on by default: a bounded cache (10,000 entries, 1 h) keyed on SHA-256 of (task id, config id, body). It matches bytes, which is what the SDK's sender re-sends on a retry (it serializes once); the same event serialized differently by another agent is not recognised. without_dedup() turns it off.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST validate the task ID matches an expected task
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. An event about any task other than the one the config was registered for (a status or artifact update, a Task, a Message with another or no task id) is refused 403 TaskMismatch.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement appropriate security measures to verify the notification source
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. receive() verifies the source by the config's notification token (either header spelling, looked up by SHA-256, compared in constant time) and its Authorization scheme and credentials; any mismatch is 401.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST attempt delivery at least once for each configured webhook
entries.notes: Every configured webhook is attempted for every event, on the background and blocking paths. push_delivery_budget now sets concurrency: ceil(configs / (budget / timeout)), at least 1, at most configs (17 at the defaults); events go in order per webhook. Until 2026-10-11 deliveries were sequential and the budget skipped the rest (6 of 100 reached at defaults). PushRetryPolicy max_attempts 0 is taken as 1 (setter and loop). Not covered: a webhook whose single attempt exceeds push_delivery_timeout is cut off, which is an attempt, not a skip.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
entries.notes: PushRetryPolicy default 3 attempts, backoff [1s,2s]; only 5xx/408/429/transport errors are retried. Tests assert 3 attempts against a failing webhook, the backoff paid between attempts and not after the last, and the default doubling [1s, 2s] schedule; shown able to fail by fixing attempts at 1 (attempt-count tests fail), removing the backoff sleep (backoff test fails) and changing the default to [1s, 1s] (default-policy test fails) (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD include a reasonable timeout for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
entries.notes: HttpPushSender's per-request timeout defaults to 10s and HandlerLimits::push_delivery_timeout, which bounds a whole delivery with its retries, to 30s: both inside the recommended 10-30s. At the defaults every attempt of the three-attempt schedule starts inside the bound (5s, 16s, 28s when each request runs to its timeout); the first two finish. Until 2026-10-12 the bound was 5s and truncated the schedule to one attempt.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
entries.notes: max_attempts per delivery; non-retryable 4xx stops immediately. push_delivery_stops_after_the_configured_number_of_failures asserts a webhook failing every attempt gets exactly 2, then exactly 5, attempts when that many are configured and the delivery is reported failed; shown able to fail by fixing the retry loop at one attempt (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Extensions SHOULD include version information in their URI identifier.
entries.notes: The five extensions the SDK authors (failure, provenance, idempotency, lease, approval; lease was missing from the count until 2026-10-20) carry /v1 in their URIs; since 2026-10-18 build() warns about a card extension URI with no version in it (no digit at all, a deliberately loose test). Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. The SDK's own extensions carry /v1, and build() reports any card extension URI without a version (tested).

entries.requirement: A new URI MUST be created for breaking changes to an extension.
impl_evidence: RELEASING.md:112 "If this release changes an extension or a binding"
entries.notes: Process requirement on extension authors. Re-examined 2026-10-18, reclassified from NOT_APPLICABLE to APPLICATION: a release-process obligation carried by RELEASING.md's checklist. Re-examined 2026-10-20, APPLICATION -> TESTED, binds agent-application -> spec-authors: the SDK is itself the author of five extensions (failure, provenance, idempotency, lease, approval; the earlier note listed four), so the obligation is its own, as the entries for the binding it authors (spec lines 479, 1194, 1279, 3214, 3216) already treat theirs. uri_contracts pins each URI to a snapshot of its wire contract (metadata key, field and variant names read from the Deserialize impls, a fully populated sample of each value, tokens and their meaning); a contract change under an unchanged URI fails, as does a bumped URI with the old snapshot. Shown failing 2026-10-20 on a renamed token, an added optional field and a bumped URI. Whether a change is breaking stays a person's call (RELEASING.md): the test makes the question unavoidable, not the answer automatic.

entries.requirement: If a client requests a version of an extension that the agent does not support, the agent SHOULD ignore the extension for that interaction and proceed without it
entries.notes: Activated set is the exact-string intersection of A2A-Extensions request header and card-declared URIs; undeclared URIs are silently ignored and not echoed.

entries.requirement: unless the extension is marked as required in the AgentCard, in which case the agent MUST return an error indicating unsupported extension
entries.notes: Handler-level check (all bindings; gRPC metadata is converted to the same header map) returns ExtensionSupportRequiredError (-32008) naming missing URIs. Note: GetExtendedAgentCard does not call ensure_required_extensions (extended_card.rs has no call).

entries.requirement: It MUST NOT fall back to a previous version of the extension automatically.
entries.notes: Extension URIs match by exact string equality: a client declaring .../v2 neither satisfies a required .../v1 nor activates an optional one. Shown to fail with version-agnostic matching injected.

entries.requirement: Identical Functionality: Provide the same set of operations and capabilities
entries.notes: All 11 operations are routed on JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC and WebSocket (TCK --equivalence). WebSocket's leftover v0.3 alias message/stream was removed on 2026-10-12 and is now -32601 as over HTTP; shown to fail with the alias restored.

entries.requirement: Consistent Behavior: Return semantically equivalent results for the same requests
entries.notes: All bindings dispatch to the same RequestHandler; TCK compares task views across the four bindings in CI. Proto3 defaults on the JSON bindings are unset on ingress since 2026-10-13, as the gRPC conversion reads them: a part's mediaType and filename, a push config's id and token, ListTasks' contextId, pageToken and status. Before, JSON read them as values: an empty mediaType was refused as ContentTypeNotSupported, a config was stored under id "", and ListTasks listed nothing, where gRPC accepted, minted an id and listed everything. Each test failed before the change. Also since 2026-10-13, a raw part that is not base64 and an integer beyond ±2^53, neither of which gRPC can carry, are refused on the JSON bindings rather than stored.

entries.requirement: Same Error Handling: Map errors consistently using appropriate protocol-specific codes
entries.notes: Single ErrorCode table drives HTTP status, gRPC code and JSON-RPC code. A malformed query value on HTTP+JSON is InvalidParams as on JSON-RPC and gRPC (2026-10-13); it was read as absent. A gRPC error carries its data as the JSON bindings do (2026-10-13): a BadRequest as google.rpc.BadRequest, any other data as a google.protobuf.Struct detail, and a stream's error as a unary call's. gRPC dropped data, and a stream's error was INTERNAL "event queue error", so a lagged stream could not be told from an executor failure; the gRPC client decodes the details back into data.

entries.requirement: Equivalent Authentication: Support the same authentication schemes declared in the AgentCard
entries.notes: Auth is enforced by handler-level interceptors common to all bindings; CI runs a secured SUT and checks rejection+acceptance on all four bindings (tck.yml:217).

entries.requirement: Agents MUST declare all supported protocols in their AgentCard
entries.notes: Declaring is the card author's. The SDK's hook is the check every listener runs when it starts, public since 2026-10-24 so that a binding outside this crate can run it too (RequestHandler::undeclared_binding, warn_if_undeclared): Server (JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON, through Dispatcher::protocol_binding), CombinedDispatcher, the axum A2aRouter, the WebSocket listener, the gRPC router build, and the SLIMRPC server (SlimRpcServer::from_app) each warn when the handler's static card declares no interface with their binding; a dynamic card is produced elsewhere and is not checked. By default a warning, because many deployments and fixtures serve a card from one listener that names others. Under ServeConfig::production() (ADR 0025, 2026-10-21) Server refuses to start and accepts nothing for an undeclared binding (tests/production_listener.rs an_undeclared_binding_is_refused_even_on_loopback); that covers Server with the JSON-RPC or REST dispatcher only, and CombinedDispatcher, the WebSocket and gRPC listeners and SLIMRPC warn without refusing. Every call site is pinned by a test that fails with the call removed (shown 2026-10-24 by removing each: the four in this crate together, and SLIMRPC's alone). History: the axum adapter did not check until 2026-10-20 and the SLIMRPC server did not until 2026-10-24; the earlier note's 'tested' covered only the predicate and the axum router (independent re-audit, 2026-10-24). Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY choose any protocol declared by the agent
entries.notes: from_card_preferring / with_protocol_binding. The tests assert from_card_preferring connects to the binding the caller ranks, not the card's first interface; shown able to fail by removing the preference sort in builder/selection.rs (both fail) (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement fallback logic for alternative protocols
entries.notes: Fallback is build-time only (next interface when the chosen one cannot be constructed); there is no runtime fallback on connection failure.

entries.requirement: All A2A-specific errors defined in Section 3.3.2 MUST be mapped to binding-specific error representations.
entries.notes: ErrorCode enum is the single source; http_status()/grpc_status() derive per-binding codes; gRPC adds google.rpc.ErrorInfo.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST define equivalent error code mappings that preserve the semantic meaning of each A2A error type.
impl_evidence: spec/slimrpc_v1/slimrpc.md:210 "A2A Error to SLIMRPC Code Mapping"
entries.notes: WebSocket reuses the JSON-RPC codes verbatim, documented in its binding spec §5. Remaining: SLIMRPC's RpcCode mapping for PushNotSupported/UnsupportedOperation/VersionNotSupported (UNIMPLEMENTED) differs from A2A §5.4's gRPC column (FAILED_PRECONDITION); this is the SLIMRPC spec's own mapping (2977, maintainer/upstream). Reclassified PARTIAL to TESTED on 2026-10-14 (audit register, the §12/§5.4 row, approved): UNIMPLEMENTED preserves the meaning the A2A types carry (the operation is not available here), as SLIMRPC's own canonical mapping requires; the difference from the gRPC column is for the maintainer to report upstream (draft prepared, not filed).

entries.requirement: The binding specification SHOULD provide a similar mapping table showing how each A2A error type is represented in the custom binding's native error format.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18, PARTIAL -> TESTED: for both custom bindings this SDK provides, its documentation carries a table of every A2A error: the WebSocket binding specification §5, and since 2026-10-18 a full fourteen-row table in the SLIMRPC crate's README, whose three rows SLIMRPC's own §6.1 omits (-32007, -32008, -32009) taking A2A §5.4's gRPC code; each is pinned by a test. What remains is upstream's, not this SDK's: the vendored SLIMRPC specification's table still lacks those three rows (docs/upstream/slimrpc-a2a-error-mapping-report.md, held by the maintainer).

entries.requirement: All JSON serializations of the A2A protocol data model MUST use camelCase naming for field names
entries.notes: All Serialize structs carry rename_all=camelCase (scripted scan found none with snake_case fields lacking it); snake_case accepted as input alias only (proto_field_alias.rs).

entries.requirement: Enum values MUST be represented according to the ProtoJSON specification ... (typically SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).
entries.notes: TaskState/Role (the only proto enums) serialize as TASK_STATE_*/ROLE_*; legacy lowercase accepted as aliases on input.

entries.requirement: Protocol Buffer enum: TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED -> JSON value: "TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED"
entries.notes: Keyword appears only inside an enum identifier in an example; covered by the §5.5 enum entry. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the keyword is descriptive here; the normative requirement is the field_behavior annotation or the neighbouring entry.

entries.requirement: When serialized to JSON ... timestamps MUST be represented as ISO 8601 formatted strings in UTC timezone.
entries.notes: Every executor event passes the queue writer, which stamps an empty status timestamp with UTC now, rewrites one with a non-Z offset to the same instant in UTC (millisecond precision), and refuses one that does not parse as ISO 8601. Until 2026-10-10 an executor-set value went out unchanged on JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket. Not covered: a Task an application writes straight to the task store, bypassing the queue. Since 2026-10-13 a timestamp is kept as written only in the canonical shape (T, Z, no offset): a lower-case t or z is rewritten as an offset is, and the parser reads RFC 3339 exactly as the gRPC conversion does, so a value served over JSON is one gRPC can carry.

entries.requirement: Millisecond precision SHOULD be used where available
entries.notes: utc_now_iso8601 formats YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ.

entries.requirement: Clients and servers MUST parse and generate ISO 8601 timestamps correctly
entries.notes: Server rejects malformed statusTimestampAfter with InvalidParams; JSON-path clients keep timestamps as opaque strings (no parsing needed). Until 2026-10-13 the parser was lenient (whitespace, unpadded or signed fields, an offset without minutes, 02-30 rolled into March) and refused every pre-1970 instant, so the JSON and gRPC bindings disagreed on such values and a 1969 statusTimestampAfter was InvalidParams. It now reads exactly what the time crate's RFC 3339 parser reads, checked over 1,655,808 strings, and the formatter writes pre-1970 instants as themselves.

entries.requirement: When millisecond precision is not available, the fractional seconds portion MAY be omitted or zero-filled
entries.notes: Parser accepts with and without fractional seconds. Asserts a timestamp with no fraction, and with .0, .000 and .000000, parses to the same millisecond instant while a non-zero fraction is read; shown able to fail by making parse_iso8601_to_unix_millis refuse a timestamp without a fraction (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Timestamps MUST NOT include timezone offsets other than 'Z' (all times are UTC)
entries.notes: Every executor event passes the queue writer, which stamps an empty status timestamp with UTC now, rewrites one with a non-Z offset to the same instant in UTC (millisecond precision), and refuses one that does not parse as ISO 8601. Until 2026-10-10 an executor-set value went out unchanged on JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket. Not covered: a Task an application writes straight to the task store, bypassing the queue. Since 2026-10-13 a timestamp is kept as written only in the canonical shape (T, Z, no offset): a lower-case t or z is rewritten as an offset is, and the parser reads RFC 3339 exactly as the gRPC conversion does, so a value served over JSON is one gRPC can carry.

entries.requirement: ...annotations to indicate whether fields are REQUIRED. These annotations serve as both documentation and validation hints
entries.notes: Descriptive; requirements are in the next entries. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the keyword is descriptive here; the normative requirement is the field_behavior annotation or the neighbouring entry.

entries.requirement: Fields marked REQUIRED indicate that the field MUST be present and set in valid messages.
entries.notes: Non-Option serde fields make absence a parse error (InvalidParams); ids validated non-empty/bounded by validate_id.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD validate these requirements and reject messages with missing required fields.
entries.notes: Inbound requests validated by typed deserialization plus explicit checks.

entries.requirement: Arrays marked as required MUST contain at least one element.
entries.notes: Enforced for Message.parts and Artifact.parts (before), and since 2026-10-11 for the published AgentCard: validate refuses empty defaultInputModes, defaultOutputModes, skills, or a skill's tags; build() runs it, the dynamic handler answers 500 for an invalid produced card, hot reload refuses one. Remaining, why PARTIAL/low: (1) ListTasksResponse.tasks is REQUIRED-repeated in the proto yet legitimately empty for a listing with no matches, a contradiction inside the specification; the SDK returns the empty list. (2) closed 2026-10-14: HotReloadAgentCardHandler::try_update validates as reload_from_json does and update is deprecated; served through DynamicAgentCardHandler, a card from new or update that does not validate is answered 500 rather than served (dynamic_handler/tests.rs an_invalid_produced_card_is_not_served). The contradiction in (1) is reported upstream by the maintainer (draft, not filed). Client-side parsing stays tolerant on purpose. Since 2026-10-13 StaticAgentCardHandler::new runs the same checks (InvalidParams); a card handed to it directly was served unchecked. Since 2026-10-14 the queue writer also refuses an executor message (event, status message, snapshot history) with no parts and a snapshot artifact with no parts (R36). Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept PARTIAL/low: every required array the SDK controls is refused empty (tested), but ListTasksResponse.tasks is REQUIRED-repeated and must be empty for a listing with no matches; the specification contradicts itself, and no SDK behaviour satisfies both (draft report held). Re-checked 2026-10-20 against upstream a2aproject/A2A main at 1205f45 (2026-10-15): spec line 1263 and a2a.proto's `repeated Task tasks = 1 [(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED]` are unchanged, and no release after v1.0.1 exists. The two readings, both in docs/upstream/a2a-required-empty-array-report.md: (a) literal, a no-match listing must answer an error §3.1.4 does not define; (b) the rule is for structural arrays, and a query result may be empty. No response satisfies both for an empty match set; the SDK follows (b).

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD ignore unrecognized fields in messages
entries.notes: No deny_unknown_fields anywhere in types/server/client src. The oneof wrappers skip unknown keys too: SendMessageResponse, StreamResponse and OAuthFlows through oneof_deserialize! (Part and SecurityScheme have their own deserializers), while still refusing no member or two. Until 2026-10-13 those three derived serde's externally tagged encoding, which failed on any key beside the member, so a response, a stream event or a card's flows carrying a field from a later version did not parse.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings SHOULD be identified by a URI.
entries.notes: WebSocket: https://a2a-rust.com/bindings/websocket/v1; SlimRPC: https://a2a-protocol.org/bindings/experimental-slimrpc/v1.

entries.requirement: The protocolBinding field in the Agent Card's supportedInterfaces entry SHOULD be a URI
entries.notes: The SDK's own custom bindings are URIs (WEBSOCKET_BINDING_URI; SLIMRPC's upstream URI), and since 2026-10-18 build() warns about a custom protocolBinding that is not a URI. The card's content stays the author's. Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY.
