impl_evidence: book/src/bindings/websocket.md:235 "## 8. Differences from the JSON-RPC HTTP binding"
spec/slimrpc_v1/slimrpc.md:1 "# SLIMRPC Custom Protocol Binding for A2A"
entries.notes: WebSocket: examples and a differences table are in the binding spec (§3, §5, §8); TCK --equivalence compares it with the spec bindings; edge cases are tested in websocket.rs and websocket_*.rs. SLIMRPC is checked against upstream's spec and the official crate. Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. As 2986.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST ensure appropriate scope limitation based on the authenticated caller's authorization boundaries. This applies to all operations that access or list tasks and other resources.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: caller isolation is on by default with an authenticating interceptor (builder.rs build) and scopes every operation to the caller's partition. The earlier note cited a function name (in_caller_partition) that does not exist; it is enter_caller_partition.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST implement authorization checks on every A2A Protocol Operations request
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: every operation on every binding runs the interceptor chain before the handler acts, and since 2026-10-18 the chain sees the task the request names (CallContext::task_id), so a per-task authorizer can be written there; the test drives all of Method::ALL on both HTTP bindings, checks the id each method exposes and that a refused task is 403. The default with identified callers authorizes per caller (caller isolation: another caller's task is TaskNotFound on every operation). A finer policy (roles, per-task ACLs) is the agent's, through ServerInterceptor; the earlier note that per-resource checks could not be written in an interceptor no longer holds.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST scope results to the caller's authorized access boundaries as defined by the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: results are scoped to the caller's partition by default once callers are identified; see §13.1 3075.

entries.requirement: Even when contextId or other filter parameters are not specified in requests, implementations MUST scope results to the caller's authorized access boundaries
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: a ListTasks with no filter returns only the caller's partition (the test lists with default params).

entries.requirement: Authorization models are agent-defined and MAY be based on: user identity, roles/groups, project/workspace, tenant boundaries, custom logic
entries.notes: MAY: multi-tenant model SUPPORTED (TenantResolver + TenantAware stores); user/role/project models only expressible as tenants or as method-level allow/deny in an interceptor; no resource-level hook. (Re-graded on 2026-10-10: a MAY takes SUPPORTED/NOT_SUPPORTED; the tenant model is supported, and the missing per-principal hook is the §13.1 entries at lines 3075-3093.) The user-identity model is now supported too: isolate_tasks_by_caller, the default with an authenticating interceptor since 2026-10-12. The tests assert the user-identity model (another caller's task is not found), the tenant model (another tenant's task is not found) and custom logic in an interceptor (one task refused 403); shown able to fail by collapsing TenantContext::partition to one partition and by hiding CallContext::task_id; roles, groups and projects remain expressible only as tenants or interceptor logic (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: List Tasks: MUST only return tasks visible to the authenticated client according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: met by caller isolation; Bob lists none of Alice's tasks.

entries.requirement: Get Task: MUST verify the authenticated client has access to the requested task according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: GetTask for another caller's task is TaskNotFound, as for an unknown id.

entries.requirement: Task-related operations (Cancel, Subscribe, Push Notification Config): MUST verify the client has appropriate access rights according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: Cancel, Subscribe and the push-config operations on another caller's task are refused as not found; a webhook Bob registers lands in his own partition.

entries.requirement: Authorization checks MUST occur before any database queries or operations that could leak information about the existence of resources outside the caller's authorization scope
entries.notes: call.before() (interceptors) and resolve_tenant/isolatable run before any task_store access in every handler; out-of-partition tasks surface as TaskNotFound, indistinguishable from nonexistent. Caveat: the CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig taskId-empty check (push_config.rs:167) runs before interceptors but reads no store. 2026-10-20: the handler/mod.rs:279 citation named a blank line above resolve_tenant; it now names resolve_tenant in handler/tenant_resolution.rs, which since today also sends its refusals through the interceptor chain before answering.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD document their authorization model and access control policies
impl_evidence: book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md:12 "Tenant identity has to come from somewhere trustworthy"
entries.notes: Deployment documentation duty; the SDK documents its own (tenant-only) model in tenant_resolver.rs module docs and book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the spec leaves the authorization model to each agent. The SDK documents the model it enforces by default, caller isolation within a tenant (book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md); the earlier wording 'tenant-only' was stale. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the caller-isolation model is documented in book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md, now the first citation.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST include authentication credentials in webhook requests as specified in PushNotificationConfig.authentication
entries.notes: The sender writes Authorization for Bearer and Basic (case-insensitive), as a2a-go v2.5.0 does. A config naming any other scheme is now refused at creation with InvalidParams, so no webhook is called without the credentials its config specifies. Until 2026-10-10 such a config was stored and delivered without credentials (a2a-go still does that). The sender's runtime drop remains for configs stored before. Since 2026-10-13 a token or credentials a header cannot carry (CR, LF or another control character) is InvalidParams at creation, inline or by CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig; it was stored and refused at every delivery.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement reasonable timeout values for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
entries.notes: Per-request timeout 10s, whole-delivery bound 30s by default, both configurable (HttpPushSender::with_timeout, HandlerLimits::with_push_delivery_timeout). The test that used to pin the two defaults contradicting each other now pins that they fit: every attempt starts, two finish.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
entries.notes: 3 attempts, backoff [1s,2s] (doubling; schedule is an explicit list whose last entry repeats, not computed exponential). Retries 5xx/408/429/transport errors only. Caveat: under the default 5s handler bound a timed-out first attempt leaves no time for retries (see 3110).

entries.requirement: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
entries.notes: Per-event max_attempts only; no cross-event circuit breaker that disables a config after N consecutive failed events. Asserts a webhook failing every attempt gets exactly the configured 2, then 5, attempts and no more; shown able to fail by fixing the retry loop at one attempt; the count is per delivery, with no cross-event circuit breaker (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD validate webhook URLs to prevent SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) attacks
entries.notes: Synchronous host check at config creation, DNS-resolve-all + IP pinning at delivery (http), cert validation defeats rebinding for https. Bypassable only by explicit HttpPushSender::allow_private_urls().
Also CGNAT, 0.0.0.0, IPv6 ULA, IPv4-mapped/NAT64 forms and inet_aton numeric encodings.

entries.requirement: Reject localhost and link-local addresses
entries.notes: localhost, *.local, *.internal hostnames and 169.254/16, fe80::/10 rejected.

entries.requirement: Implement URL allowlists where appropriate
entries.notes: Opt-in HttpPushSender::with_allowed_hosts: exact host match, ignoring case and port, no wildcards. Enforced at config creation (InvalidParams) and again at delivery before any connection. Custom senders can answer PushSender::allows_webhook_url (default true).

entries.requirement: Clients MUST validate webhook authenticity using the provided authentication credentials
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. The config's authentication credentials are checked against the request's one Authorization header (scheme case-insensitive, credentials in constant time); register() refuses a config that names authentication but carries no credentials, so the check cannot be silently skipped.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD verify the task ID in the payload matches an expected task they created
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. See §4.3.3 879: a foreign or missing task id is 403.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. See §4.3.3 877.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. See §4.3.3 878.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent webhook flooding
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. with_rate_limit(per_sec, burst) gives each registered config a token bucket, checked after authentication so a request without the config's secrets cannot spend its allowance; past it, 429, which the SDK's sender retries. Off by default: a rate is the deployment's to choose.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use HTTPS endpoints for webhook URLs to ensure confidentiality
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. The client checks the webhook URL of set_push_config and of a send carrying an inline push config: an http:// URL to a non-loopback host is logged at WARN by default and, with ClientBuilder::require_https_webhooks(), refused before sending (ClientError::InsecureWebhook, carrying only the origin).

entries.requirement: Webhook URLs SHOULD use HTTPS to protect payload confidentiality in transit
entries.notes: HTTPS delivery supported (tls-rustls feature, on by default via sdk) and tested over real TLS. Since 2026-10-12 opt-in HttpPushSender::https_only() refuses an http:// webhook at config creation (InvalidParams naming the reason, via PushSender::requires_https) and again at delivery before any connection, as the opt-in allowlist (line 3116) does for hosts. Off by default: plain http is still accepted unless a deployment sets it. Before: no option enforced https.

entries.requirement: Authentication tokens in PushNotificationConfig SHOULD be treated as secrets and rotated periodically
entries.notes: Secret handling (Debug redaction, origin-only URL logging) tested; rotation is an application duty (re-create config). The background delivery's failure and timeout WARNs logged the whole webhook URL, path and query included, until 2026-10-14 (audit register R14); they now log its origin, as the sender's own lines did. v1.0.1's text names PushNotificationConfig, which the v1.0.1 proto does not define: the message with `authentication` is TaskPushNotificationConfig (a2a.proto line 469), the name upstream main uses since.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD securely store push notification configurations and credentials
entries.notes: Opt-in, since 2026-10-12: given a PushConfigCipher (with_cipher), the four SQL push-config stores write each config sealed (the whole JSON, so token and authentication.credentials are never stored in the clear) as a2a-sealed:v1:<base64>, bound as associated data to its row (partition, task id, config id), so a sealed config moved to another row does not open; with a cipher an unsealed row is refused unless accept_unsealed_rows, and without one a sealed row is refused. The SDK ships no cipher (tests use AES-256-GCM from ring). Default stores still write plaintext JSON; in-memory stores and Debug output are redacted as before.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use unique, single-purpose tokens for each push notification configuration
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client crate now ships a2a_protocol_client::webhook::WebhookReceiver (feature webhook, on by default in the client and the SDK). A receiving application that hands each request's headers and body to receive() gets this check; one that writes its own receiver keeps the duty. webhook::new_notification_token() returns 244 random bits as 43 base64url characters, one per config; WebhookReceiver::register() refuses a token another registered config already uses (TokenInUse).

entries.requirement: The Get Extended Agent Card operation MUST require authentication
entries.notes: Refused unless an interceptor reporting authenticates()==true is registered, or the operator opts out with allow_unauthenticated_extended_card(). The check applies to an extended card set with with_extended_agent_card too, with or without a public card on the handler.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST authenticate requests using one of the schemes declared in the public AgentCard.securitySchemes and AgentCard.security fields
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-18 build() asks every authenticating interceptor, through ServerInterceptor::checks_scheme, whether it checks each scheme the public and extended cards declare, and refuses one that checks none of them: a client following the card could never pass it. Bearer and JWT check the HTTP bearer scheme and OAuth 2.0/OIDC (bearer access tokens); ApiKey checks an apiKey scheme in its header (case-insensitive). A custom interceptor that does not answer (None) is not checked; that residual is the integrator's. A card that declares no schemes is not refused (warned nowhere): nothing to compare against.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY return different extended card content based on the authenticated client's identity or authorization level
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 an ExtendedCardProvider (RequestHandlerBuilder::with_extended_card_provider) chooses each caller's extended card from the configured one, after the interceptor chain authenticated the request, or refuses the caller. Its card is checked as build() checks the configured one (valid, push notifications only with a push sender, the server's extensions advertised, refused when signed without them). Before: one extended card (with_extended_agent_card) for every authenticated caller. The tests assert each authenticated caller is served the card the ExtendedCardProvider chooses for it, or refused; shown able to fail by making for_caller ignore the provider (six tests fail) (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate caching headers to control client-side caching of extended cards
entries.notes: GET /extendedAgentCard (RestDispatcher and the axum router) sends Cache-Control: private, no-cache, Vary: Authorization and an ETag over the serialized card, and answers 304 to a matching If-None-Match. JSON-RPC, gRPC and WebSocket fetch the card over POST or a stream, where HTTP caching headers do not apply.

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY include additional skills not present in the public card
entries.notes: with_extended_agent_card serves a card with skills the public one lacks; the test adds one. Until 2026-10-14 the public and extended card were the same (audit register R56). Asserts the extended card served to an authenticated caller has a skill the public card lacks; shown able to fail by serving the public card in its place (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY expose more detailed capability information (e.g., rate limits, quotas)
entries.notes: The extended card is any valid card the operator sets, capabilities included; build() advertises this server's extensions on it as on the public card. Until 2026-10-14 there was one card. Asserts over HTTP+JSON that /extendedAgentCard carries a quotas extension (requestsPerMinute, monthlyTasks) that the public well-known card lacks; shown able to fail by serving the public card in place of the extended one (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY include organization-specific or user-specific configuration
entries.notes: Organization-specific content in the one extended card (with_extended_agent_card); user-specific content needs per-caller variation, which the handler does not provide (3144). Asserts an ExtendedCardProvider gives alice and bob each an extended card carrying their own workspace configuration; shown able to fail by making for_caller ignore the provider; the note that per-caller variation is not provided is out of date since the 3144 provider (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD document which capabilities are available at different authentication levels
entries.notes: Operator documentation duty. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: what each authentication level unlocks is the agent's policy; the SDK serves the machine-readable form (with_extended_agent_card, ExtendedCardProvider).

entries.requirement: Extended cards SHOULD NOT include sensitive information that could be exploited if leaked (e.g., internal service URLs, unmasked credentials)
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the extended card goes through the same checks as the public one (see §14 3341): an unmasked credential in a URL is refused at build() and by per-caller extended cards, and an internal service URL is reported by card_warnings. Residual, the author's: free text is not inspected.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST validate that clients have appropriate permissions before returning privileged information in extended cards
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the extended card is served only through the interceptor chain and only with an authenticating interceptor (unless allow_unauthenticated_extended_card); ExtendedCardProvider chooses, or refuses, each caller's card. Which permission unlocks what is the agent's policy, expressed in the provider.

entries.requirement: Clients retrieving extended cards SHOULD replace their cached public Agent Card with the extended version for the duration of their authenticated session
entries.notes: The SDK caches a card in two places. A2aClient caches the capabilities it checks calls against (DeclaredCapabilities, from the card it was built from); since 2026-10-13 get_extended_agent_card replaces them with the extended card's (A2aClient::adopt_capabilities), keeping extendedAgentCard declared, and only when the client checks at all. Before, it kept the public card's, so a capability only the extended card declared was refused locally with CapabilityNotDeclared. The other, the resolver's, is replaced when the application calls CachingCardResolver::install_extended_card, which serves the extended card from resolve() until clear_extended_card() or invalidate(); the application decides when the session ends.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD version extended cards appropriately and honor client cache invalidation
entries.notes: card.version stays operator-set. Cache invalidation is honoured through revalidation: no-cache makes the client check every use, and the ETag changes whenever the card does (a new version included, tested), so a stale cached card is replaced on the next request.

entries.requirement: When capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, the operation MUST return UnsupportedOperationError
entries.notes: Not declared by the handler's card: UnsupportedOperationError. No card on the handler at all and no extended card: UnsupportedOperationError too, since 2026-10-14 (the register's §13.3 row, approved); it answered ExtendedAgentCardNotConfigured, asserting a declaration the handler cannot see. A handler with no public card but an extended card serves it (the card published elsewhere declares the capability).

entries.requirement: When support is declared but no extended card is configured, the operation MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError
entries.notes: Declared by the handler's card with no with_extended_agent_card: ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError, since 2026-10-14 (audit register R68). Until then this entry was TESTED on the no-card path, the only one that returned -32007; a declared card with no extended card served the public card instead, which this MUST forbids. The test failed before the change.

entries.requirement: Production deployments MUST use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC)
entries.notes: Same requirement as §7.1. Every SDK listener can terminate TLS (Server::with_tls for HTTP, WebSocketDispatcher::with_tls since 2026-10-18, GrpcDispatcher::with_tls) and the client reaches https:// and wss:// with verified roots. Using them in production is the deployment's duty. The earlier note (the built-in hyper serve()/WebSocket listeners are plaintext only) was stale for HTTP since Server::with_tls (2026-10-14) and is fixed for WebSocket; serve()/serve_with_addr themselves stay plaintext and run on Server since 2026-10-18, so TLS is Server::bind(..).with_tls(..). Status corrected 2026-10-18 from SUPPORTED, which the ledger reserves for MAY. As 1879. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): every TLS entry point named re-checked; the stray 'SUPPORTED' wording removed (the status is APPLICATION); Server::with_tls's line re-pointed. Since 2026-10-20 Server also warns once at start when it serves plaintext on an address that is not loopback (serve/graceful/plaintext.rs plaintext_warning); a warning, because TLS is often terminated in front. Since 2026-10-21 (ADR 0025) ServeConfig::production() makes Server refuse to start on plaintext beyond loopback, accepting nothing, unless with_tls_terminated_in_front is set (tests/production_listener.rs plaintext_beyond_loopback_is_refused_and_nothing_is_accepted, tls_terminated_in_front_serves_beyond_loopback); the refusal and the plaintext warning are Server's alone: the WebSocket and gRPC listeners neither warn about plaintext nor refuse it, and CombinedDispatcher is not covered by the refusal. Re-audited 2026-10-24: the sentence binds the deployment, since what 'production' means is the deployer's; this entry and the one for the same sentence at §7.1/§13.4 carry the same binds.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD enforce HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) headers when using HTTP-based bindings
entries.notes: Opt-in dispatch::Hsts wraps any Dispatcher and sets Strict-Transport-Security on every response, errors included. Browsers ignore HSTS over plain HTTP (RFC 6797 §8.1), so it takes effect on a TLS listener: Server::with_tls (since 2026-10-14) or a TLS terminator in front; axum users add it with their own middleware. Not on by default: a header claiming HTTPS on a plaintext deployment would be wrong. (Until 2026-10-18 this note said the built-in listener is plaintext, which Server::with_tls had made stale.)

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD disable support for deprecated SSL/TLS versions (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1)
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST validate all input parameters before processing
entries.notes: Protocol-level validation (ids, metadata size, timestamps, page size clamp, push URL) in the SDK; validation of message content semantics is the executor's. Detailed per-field validation is covered by other sections' audits. A GET's query parameters on the HTTP+JSON binding are validated since 2026-10-13: a historyLength, pageSize, status or includeArtifacts that does not parse is InvalidParams (400) on RestDispatcher and A2aRouter alike, where it was read as absent.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate limits on message sizes, file sizes, and request complexity
entries.notes: Body cap (4 MiB default), gRPC message cap, WS frame cap, metadata/id/parts/artifacts caps. A body not received within body_read_timeout is 408 on HTTP+JSON (the axum router's answer too) since 2026-10-13; every body read failure was 413 there, a stalled upload included. A body stream hyper cannot read is 400. JSON-RPC answers either with -32700.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD sanitize or validate file content types and reject unexpected media types
entries.notes: Part mediaType checked against card defaultInputModes/skill inputModes; parts without mediaType and content sniffing are not checked (content sanitization is the executor's).

entries.requirement: API keys, tokens, and other credentials MUST be treated as secrets
entries.notes: Constant-time comparison, Debug shows counts not keys, identity labels separate from credentials, push secrets redacted. Exception: SQL push-config stores keep credentials plaintext at rest (see 3131). Client: until 2026-10-14 (audit register R17) the derived Debug of ClientRequest, ClientResponse, CardFetchOptions and WebSocketTransportConfig printed header values (the Authorization an auth interceptor adds) and push-config params and results verbatim; they print header names and JSON keys now, never values.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be rotated periodically
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: every credential the SDK checks can now be rotated while serving. The static bearer and API-key interceptors hand out a CredentialSet (credentials()) whose add/add_labelled/revoke apply from the next request (the test overlaps old and new, then retires the old); a remote JWKS is refetched on key rotation; the client's token providers refresh and drop a token answered 401. How often to rotate is the operator's schedule.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be transmitted only over encrypted connections
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: both directions in which the SDK sends a credential now act on plaintext. Client: a call carrying Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie or an AuthInterceptor::api_key header or query parameter to an http:// or ws:// endpoint on a non-loopback host is logged once, and refused before sending with ClientBuilder::require_https_credentials() (InsecureTransport, naming the header and origin only). Server: a push config whose token or credentials go to an http:// webhook is logged at creation (origin only), and refused with HttpPushSender::https_only(). Both refusals are opt-in, the SHOULD's latitude: loopback and lab deployments use plaintext. Residual: a gRPC endpoint given as a bare host:port carries no scheme and is not classified.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement credential revocation mechanisms
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: CredentialSet::revoke removes a static bearer token or API key while the server runs, and its next request is refused 401 (the test revokes and re-checks over JSON-RPC). JWTs are revoked by removing the signing key from the JWKS (refetched on rotation) or by exp; JwtAuthInterceptor keeps no list of revoked token ids (jti), so revoking one JWT before its exp, without rotating its key, takes a custom interceptor.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD log authentication failures
entries.notes: With the `audit` feature + with_audit, refused calls are recorded (test sends a credential-less call and asserts a record with no actor). The auth interceptors themselves emit no log line; metrics on_error counts failures.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent brute-force attacks
entries.notes: Opt-in, since 2026-10-12: AuthFailureThrottle, registered before the authenticating interceptor, counts per peer the calls refused as unauthenticated and, once a peer reaches max_failures in a window, refuses its calls as rate-limited (HTTP+JSON 429 with Retry-After, JSON-RPC -32603 and gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with RetryInfo) until the window ends, the right credential included. The peer is CallContext::peer_addr, which every binding but SLIMRPC records when the SDK serves it (axum: with ConnectInfo or a PeerAddr extension), or the client address trusted x-forwarded-for hops name; SLIMRPC records no peer, and since 2026-10-14 drops a caller's x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip and forwarded (audit register R41), which with trusted hops let a caller pick its own key, so an unidentified SLIMRPC caller is not throttled until the binding records a verified peer (R13); at most max_peers are tracked, failing open beyond. A default server throttles nothing. RateLimitInterceptor limits throughput per caller and does not use the peer address.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD log security-relevant events (authentication failures, authorization denials, suspicious requests)
entries.notes: Opt-in audit feature records every call with outcome.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement monitoring for unusual patterns (rapid task creation, excessive cancellations)
entries.notes: SDK exposes Metrics (on_request/on_error/on_latency per method) and OTel; anomaly detection is the operator's. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: what counts as unusual is deployment policy. The SDK emits the signals: per-method Metrics, ServerInterceptor::on_complete with the caller, OTel spans and metrics, RateLimitInterceptor, AuthFailureThrottle. Re-verified against the code 2026-10-20 (ledger audit): the citation named a ListTasks log line; it now names the signals the note lists. Re-audited 2026-10-24: RateLimitInterceptor and AuthFailureThrottle refuse requests and neither logs nor calls Metrics itself, so their refusals show through the generic on_error and the audit log; Metrics::on_request is per method, per-caller counts need on_complete or the audit log.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD provide audit trails for sensitive operations
entries.notes: Hash-chained per-tenant audit log (feature `audit`, opt-in).

entries.requirement: Logs MUST NOT include sensitive information (credentials, personal data) unless required and properly protected
entries.notes: Message content capture in spans defaults off (SpanSettings.content=false); audit records digests not content.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement rate limiting on all operations
entries.notes: Opt-in interceptor; applies to every operation since the chain runs on all handlers.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD return appropriate error responses when rate limits are exceeded
entries.notes: RateLimitInterceptor refuses with A2aError::rate_limited, retrying when the window ends: HTTP+JSON 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After, gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and a google.rpc.RetryInfo detail on JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, WebSocket and gRPC; the SLIMRPC binding answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED without it (no details field). The JSON-RPC code stays -32603, the code §3.3.2 (spec line 536) gives as its example for 'rate limit exceeded'. Until 2026-10-10 the refusal was a plain internal error (500 / INTERNAL), indistinguishable from a server fault. The WebSocket binding sends the JSON-RPC error object HTTP does (sse::jsonrpc_error_from), RetryInfo included, since 2026-10-11; no test throttles a WebSocket call.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement different rate limits for different operations or user tiers
entries.notes: Per-tenant allowance (tiers via tenant config) supported; no per-operation limits in the built-in limiter (custom interceptor can key on ctx.method()). Asserts under one RateLimitInterceptor a free tenant (1 rps) is admitted 60 requests per 60s window and a premium tenant (3 rps) 180; shown able to fail by skipping the per-tenant allowance (free admitted all 1000); per-operation limits still need a custom interceptor (2026-10-20).

entries.requirement: Agents MUST comply with applicable data protection regulations
entries.notes: Legal/operational duty; not SDK-testable. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: legal compliance belongs to the deployment and cannot be established by a library; the SDK's means are EncryptedTaskStore, PushConfigCipher, AuditLog::with_privacy and the retention purges.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD provide mechanisms for users to request deletion of their data
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: since caller isolation gives each identified caller partitions of its own (the default with an authenticating interceptor), the SDK has a per-user deletion mechanism: erase_caller(identity) on every tenant-aware task and push-config store removes the caller's partitions in every tenant (tasks, logged events, idempotency keys, webhooks), in one transaction on SQLite and PostgreSQL, and reports partitions and rows; AuditLog::erase_subject erases the caller from audit records. Tested on all three backends (the PostgreSQL test runs where A2A_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set; run 2026-10-18 against a local server). Residual, the operator's: how a user's request reaches the operator (no A2A operation exists for it), records left in a tenant's shared partition (unidentified callers, or share_tasks_across_callers), and copies in backups and logs.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate data retention policies
entries.notes: In-memory TTL default 1h; persistent stores keep everything unless purge_expired is configured (documented decision); audit has its own retention.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD minimize logging of sensitive or personal information
entries.notes: Span content capture off by default; webhook URLs logged as origin only.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST address security considerations in their specification
